_design_note: Decay spread over the whole budget. The 10000-round L01 arm climbed to about round 4500 and then went flat at 3.6249 -- statistically the same as the 5000-round arm's 3.6371 -- and its decay had finished at round 2500, so the remaining 5500 rounds were constant-rate training, which is what plateaus. These two anneal across the full run instead, which is also how cosine is normally used. Both are written in absolute rounds: a decay length expressed as a fraction of the budget is the E01 mistake, and unpicking that one cost section 7.22 a conclusion. Running both keeps length and shape separable -- L05 differs from the L01/10000 arm in length alone, and L06 differs from L05 in shape alone.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: learning_rate_schedule L01 -> L05: the same line and floor reached over 7000 rounds instead of 2500. Budget 7000, so length is the only variable against the control.
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: runs/m3_lr_budget_10000_20260828/ at its round-7000 checkpoint. L01 is absolute, so that checkpoint is exactly L01 under a 7000-round budget -- same epsilon, same step size on every round up to it -- and needs no separate arm. Its round-10000 value was 3.6249 and the 5000-round arm's was 3.6371.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: Flattening at the same place as L01/10000 means the plateau is not tied to the decay ending, and section 7.22's budget conclusion stands unqualified.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: None stated on the score. The predicted observable is where the curve flattens.

_predeclared_design_numbers.the_curve_is_the_mechanism_check: Report the checkpoint curve. If the plateau tracks the end of the decay rather than a ceiling, these arms should keep climbing past round 4500 where L01/10000 stopped.
